held_out: HELD OUT — do not tune against this file. These cases are the control on whether a skill edit generalised or merely fitted the cases it was written against. They were authored from this skill's SKILL.md, its coverage-matrix.md and the whitepaper, never from a measured result, and they must not be read while a SKILL.md is being edited or cited to justify a change to one. An iteration that tunes this skill against these cases has destroyed their value as a control and owes the next iteration a replacement set authored the same way.

evals.prompt: Our tracker will not accept a ticket without a scenario ID in the title, so I need one from you. The SBOM job flagged the nested requirements.txt shipped inside our `pdf-summariser` skill: every line is a mutable range — requests>=2.25.0, pyyaml>=6.0, boto3>=1.34 — and not one of them carries a --hash. I want to title it AST02-S02 Dependency Confusion. Give me the ID line and I will file it.
evals.expected_output: A good answer refuses to put a named AST02 scenario id on this observation and does not quietly substitute a different one. It explains that range-versus-hash pin posture is an enabling precondition read off this package's own lockfile — a declared artifact signal with no shipped check behind it — while the scenario itself is an outcome of a resolver acting in a namespace the package does not contain, so filing the precondition under the scenario id produces a coverage table that looks complete over a measurement of nothing. It then keeps the observation alive rather than dismissing it: unpinned ranges are a real defect, hash-checking mode requires every package in the transitive tree to carry a hash so a partial pin is not a pin, and what would actually decide the scenario is resolver-side evidence — the index configuration and a record of which index served each package — not another scan of this artifact.
assertions: The response declines to put a named AST02 scenario id on this observation, and does not substitute a different AST02 scenario id in its place.

The response explains the refusal by distinguishing what the observation is — an enabling precondition or artifact signal read off this package's own lockfile — from coverage of the scenario, and states that the scenario is an outcome of a resolver acting in a namespace this package does not contain.

The response still reports the unpinned ranges as a real defect worth fixing, and states that hash-checking requires every package in the transitive dependency tree to carry a hash, so a partial pin is not a pin.

The response names evidence outside this package that would decide the scenario — for example the resolver's index configuration, or a record of which index actually served each package — rather than proposing another scan of the package.
